findings.finding: The multi-project inbound fetch child scopes JQL fan-out and the truncation ceiling per project but does not address the three per-project enrichment passes the current fetcher runs (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map), each of which takes exactly one project key; fanning out the base JQL while leaving enrichment single-project silently drops inbound parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Multi-project inbound fetch'; vs src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:593-718 (_build_snapshot enrichment)
findings.suggested_fix: Have _build_snapshot iterate the configured project set for the enrichment step too — call get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map once per project and merge each result — and add the multi-project enrichment fidelity to the two-project fetch acceptance test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend child 1734 to fan get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map across every configured project (one call per project, merged into the shared snapshot keyed by issue) and add the per-project-enrichment assertion to its two-project acceptance test, per parent AC2.
evidence: Parent AC2 (condensed): 'checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot'.

Parent decomposition, Multi-project inbound fetch bullet: 'the three per-project enrichment passes (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map) also fan across every configured project ... Enrichment fidelity joins the two-project fetch acceptance test.'
Child 1734 Approach: 'call the existing jqls_for once per project ... and union the results into the snapshot' — enrichment is never mentioned in its Approach, Testing, or any of its 5 ACs.

fetcher.py:593-600,647-648,688-692 — get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map are each called ONCE against a single project_key derived from _query_project or the first snapshot key; a multi-project snapshot would enrich only one project.
No other sibling in the roster names get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map or per-project enrichment fan-out.
findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot', but child 1734 — the sole child owning fetcher.py — covers only the JQL-search fan-out and never fans out the three enrichment passes.
scenarios: A store maps REB and DIG; the fetch fans JQL over both, but enrichment runs only for the first project_key, so DIG tickets silently lose parent/comment/issuelink data every pass — and the outbound differ then treats those absent maps as authoritative removals.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to child 1734's Approach and ACs an explicit per-project enrichment fan-out (loop the three map calls over the configured project set, merging each into the shared snapshot) and an AC asserting both projects' parent/comment/issuelink data are present in the merged snapshot.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign — to child 462d or 67f9 — the change making write_compat_record compute required_capabilities from the mapping and _store_compat_unit re-stamp on a desired-set mismatch in BOTH directions (add at second project, remove on drop back to one), with a test covering both transitions.
evidence: Parent decomposition: 'change _store_compat_unit's check-then-act from "blob absent" to "committed required_capabilities != desired set from the mapping" (today it never re-stamps a converged store, so it could neither add the capability at a second project nor remove it on the reverse transition); write_compat_record computes the capability list; test covers BOTH transitions.'

Child 462d Approach: stamps 'When — and only when — the mapping holds more than one project, add multi-project-bridge' and 'A single-project store is never stamped' — additive only; no de-stamp on transition back to one project. Its AC: 'The capability is stamped only when the mapping holds more than one project.'
Child 67f9 Approach: 'Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story' — scope is compat.py registration/classification only; it does not modify write_compat_record.
compat.py:325-327 — write_compat_record hardcodes 'required_capabilities': []; it does not compute the list from the mapping.

init.py:522-534 — _store_compat_unit uses the blob-absent check-then-act the decomposition says must be replaced; no child scopes init.py for this change (462d scopes project_ensures.py + ensures.py; 67f9 scopes compat.py).
findings.finding: The parent decomposition's 'Store-compat capability stamp' child requires changing _store_compat_unit from 'blob absent' to a 'committed required_capabilities != desired set' check that covers BOTH the add-at-second-project AND remove-on-reverse transitions, with write_compat_record computing the capability list and a test covering BOTH transitions — but no child in the roster owns the reverse (de-stamp) transition or the write_compat_record list computation.
scenarios: An operator removes a project from a multi-project store, dropping it back to one project; the capability entry is never removed, so an older binary keeps refusing writes to a store that is once again single-project-safe.

462d's additive stamp relies on writing multi-project-bridge into required_capabilities, but write_compat_record (owned via compat.py by 67f9, which leaves it inert) still writes [], leaving the actual list-computation seam unowned.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 462d's capability-stamp unit to compute the desired capability set from the mapping and re-write .store-compat.json whenever the committed set differs (covering both add and remove), and add its ACs for the reverse transition; correspondingly widen 67f9 or 462d to own the write_compat_record list computation in compat.py.

findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires that one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot, but child 1734 — the sibling the parent decomposition assigns this to ('Enrichment fidelity joins the two-project fetch acceptance test') — carries no acceptance criterion, approach note, or scope line covering enrichment fan-out. Its ACs cover only the JQL pair per project and the recorded project/repos. No other sibling covers per-project enrichment either.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 1734's Approach/Scope to fan get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map across every configured project (one call each per project, merged keyed by issue) and add an acceptance criterion asserting the per-project enrichment call count and both projects' enrichment data in the merged snapshot, matching parent AC2's wording.

findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion 2 requires that 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot' — but the multi-project inbound fetch child (1734) covers only the JQL-pair fan-out and source-project recording; its acceptance criteria say nothing about the three per-project enrichment passes. No sibling covers the enrichment remainder, so this half of AC2 is uncovered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion to child 1734 asserting one enrichment call per configured project for each of get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map with both projects' data merged into the snapshot, and add the enrichment merge site (fetcher._build_snapshot:577-685) to its scope; this also closes the G4 owned-by-none gap on the enrichment merge that both 1734 and a33c touch but neither owns.

findings.finding: The parent decomposition names a distinct 'Store-compat capability stamp' child whose defining behaviour is changing _store_compat_unit's check-then-act to re-stamp on divergence so it can BOTH add multi-project-bridge at a second project AND remove it on the reverse transition, 'test covers BOTH transitions.' No sibling in the roster owns the reverse (removal) transition. Child 462d only stamps (adds) the capability when the mapping holds more than one project; it never tests removal when a store drops back to one project. Child 67f9 only registers the capability name and tests fail-closed reads, not stamping. The reverse-transition behaviour is owned by NO sibling.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend child 462d's stamp unit to compute required_capabilities from the mapping on every sweep (re-stamp when committed set != desired, covering removal) with a paired both-transitions AC, or add the missing standalone 'Store-compat capability stamp' child named in the parent decomposition with that behaviour and test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that the desired-capability set is computed by the non-leaf caller (init._store_compat_unit reads .bridge_state/projects.json) and PASSED INTO write_compat_record, keeping compat.py a stdlib+fsutil leaf and preserving the lock import-cycle invariant.
evidence: compat.py docstring: 'Leaf module — stdlib + rebar._store.fsutil ONLY, no other rebar.* imports … a rebar._commands.* / rebar.config import here would create an import cycle. Keep it leaf.'
Plan: "write_compat_record computes the capability list" and "'committed required_capabilities' != desired set from the mapping"
_store_compat_unit lives in rebar._commands.init (init.py:509), which is NOT leaf and can freely read the mapping
findings.finding: The plan says write_compat_record 'computes the capability list' and the store-compat unit compares the committed required_capabilities against 'the desired set from the mapping', but does not state WHICH module reads .bridge_state/projects.json — and compat.py is a documented strict leaf module (stdlib + fsutil only, no other rebar.* imports, to avoid the lock import cycle).
scenarios: Implementer adds a mapping read inside write_compat_record and reintroduces the lock<->compat import cycle the leaf invariant exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Have _store_compat_unit (in _commands/init.py) read the mapping and pass the desired required_capabilities list as an argument to write_compat_record; do not import the mapping/projects module from compat.py.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The final AC requires that a multi-project store 'carries multi-project-bridge' so an older binary refuses writes, but the capability stamp is only (re)written by _store_compat_unit, which runs solely inside run_ensures (init / MCP-boot / fsck --repair) — NOT on every covered write. A `bridge projects` set that adds a second project mutates the mapping without necessarily triggering an ensure sweep, so the .store-compat.json stamp lags the mapping's multi-project state until the next sweep. During that window a store is genuinely multi-project yet un-stamped, and an older binary is not gated — the very duplication failure the Compatibility section says the stamp prevents.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (final) + 'Compatibility and rollback'; interaction of bridge projects command with _store_compat_unit / ensures.run_ensures

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering the ticket repos field (inbound defaulting from the mapping and create-time arg read-back).
evidence: Child: 'Ticket repos field — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.'
AC2 verifies 'the recorded project on each created ticket' (project field), not the repos field.
No AC references repos-field defaulting or read-back.
findings.finding: The 'Ticket repos field' child delivers a schema field, reducer, create-time arg and inbound defaulting from the mapping, but no acceptance criterion verifies the repos field is recorded or defaulted.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion for the promote-only rule: changing the project of an already-bound ticket is rejected while promoting from absent/empty is allowed.
evidence: Child: 'promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket)'.
The 7 ACs cover empty-project (AC3), explicit-project create (AC4), guard, migration, compat — none asserts that changing the project of a bound ticket is rejected.
findings.finding: The 'Ticket project field' child states a 'promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket)', but no acceptance criterion verifies this immutability constraint.
scenarios: An attempt to reassign a bound ticket's project would silently succeed if the promote-only rule regresses.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'disjoint file sets' claim with the two field children sharing ticket_state.schema.json and reducer/ — either merge them into one child or sequence them and drop the disjointness claim for that pair.
evidence: Header: 'Child decomposition (disjoint file sets; no edit conflicts)'.
Both children name schema + reducer + create-time args; Scope groups 'reducer/, schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, _commands/composer.py, _lib_writes.py, _mcp_writes.py — the two new ticket fields'.
findings.finding: The decomposition claims 'disjoint file sets; no edit conflicts', yet the 'Ticket project field' and 'Ticket repos field' children both edit schemas/ticket_state.schema.json and reducer/, and the Scope section lists both under the same files.
findings.location: Child decomposition header vs 'Ticket project field' / 'Ticket repos field' children
scenarios: Parallel execution of the two field children produces merge conflicts in the shared schema and reducer files, contradicting the no-edit-conflicts guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge 'Ticket project field' and 'Ticket repos field' into one 'Ticket project/repos fields' child, or declare an explicit ordering dependency between them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Docs+ADR child, commit the ADR to a short prior-art comparison against established multi-project bidirectional tracker-sync tools (e.g. Exalate/Unito) and against the internal ADR 0028 'membership is not value' invariant, justifying the store-owned project-set design as novel rather than a repackaging of filter-scoped sync state.
evidence: Bright-line fires: external Jira integration + store migration + a many-to-many project mapping the plan frames as novel ('Model many-to-many as one shared ticket store between N repos and N tracker projects').

Retrieved external prior art shows an established field of bidirectional multi-project tracker sync: Exalate (docs.exalate.com 'Sync Multiple Projects & Issue Types'), Unito ('sync multiple Jira projects'), Ticketize.it, Getint, ConnectAll.

The repo already maintains docs/oss-comparison-and-remediation.md positioning rebar against comparable trackers, but the plan's ADR deliverable does not reference it or the external multi-project-sync field.

The plan's central justification — avoiding cross-repo 'remote deletions' from a shared prev_snapshot — is the same class of problem these tools handle via filter/entity-scoped sync state, and it maps to the codebase's own ADR 0028 ('membership is not value'); the ADR asserts novelty without an anti-repackaging check against either.
findings.finding: The Docs+ADR child does not commit to considering external prior art for many-to-many multi-project tracker sync, though a mature field of bidirectional multi-project sync tools exists and the repo maintains an OSS-comparison doc for exactly this positioning.
scenarios: Reviewers assessing whether the store-owned project-set design is genuinely novel or repackages established multi-project-sync filter-scoping.
A future maintainer wanting to know why rebar's mapping differs from Exalate/Unito's approach.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance note to the 'Docs + ADR' child requiring the ADR to (a) cite how the established multi-project-sync tools model the project↔container mapping and avoid cross-scope deletion, and (b) explain why rebar's store-owned project set is the warranted choice for a shared event-sourced store rather than a per-repo/per-filter list, referencing ADR 0028.
